source.document: FTC Guides Concerning Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising, 16 CFR Part 255

rules.rule_text: Endorsements must reflect the endorser's honest opinions/experience; an endorser who claims to use the product must be a bona fide user.
rules.verbatim_quote: the endorser must have been a bona fide user of it at the time the endorsement was given

detection.logic: If the text contains first-person use claims (I take|I use|I've been using|I was prescribed|my <brand>) and meta.endorser_verified_user is not true -> fail (verification record missing).

source.document: FTC Guides Concerning Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising, 16 CFR Part 255

rules.rule_text: A consumer testimonial on a key attribute implies typical results; the advertiser needs substantiation or must clearly disclose generally expected results. 'Results not typical' does not cure.
rules.verbatim_quote: An advertisement containing an endorsement relating the experience of one or more consumers on a central or key attribute of the product will likely be interpreted as representing that the endorser's experience is representative

detection.logic: Flag first-person outcome claims (worked for me|I (lost|cleared|haven't had|feel)|my (skin|pain|migraines?) (is|are|was) (gone|clear)|for me, it works within) unless a quantitative 'generally expected results' disclosure (\d+% of (patients|people)) is present; 'results not typical/may vary' alone does not pass.

source.document: FTC Guides Concerning Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising, 16 CFR Part 255

rules.rule_text: Material connections between endorser and seller (payment, free product, employment, family) must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously.
rules.verbatim_quote: such connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously

detection.logic: If meta.endorser_compensated (or text has partner(ed)? with|teamed up with|ambassador|sponsored) require an explicit disclosure token near the start: #ad|#sponsored|paid partnership|paid (spokesperson|by)|sponsored by|compensated|in partnership with <company>.

rules.note: OPDP letters on influencer/celebrity content cite FD&C risk omission, not FTC 255; no OPDP exemplar is labeled as an FTC violation.

rules.rule_text: Health claims require competent and reliable scientific evidence matching the claim (randomized, controlled human clinical testing for most health benefit claims).
rules.verbatim_quote: supplements, drugs, and other health-related products require substantiation in the form of competent and reliable scientific evidence
rules.applies_to: DTC (FTC jurisdiction: OTC, devices, supplements, telehealth/compounders; Rx ads overlap with FDA)

detection.question: Is each health-benefit claim supported by evidence of the type and quality the claim implies?
detection.pass_anchor: Claim scope matches RCT evidence on the claimed endpoint and population.
detection.fail_anchor: Claim implies outcomes, populations or magnitudes beyond the evidence.

rules.rule_text: Qualifying information needed to prevent deception must be clear, conspicuous, simple and close to the claim; vague qualifiers ('may', 'helps') are inadequate.

detection.question: Where a claim needs qualification, is the qualifier specific, prominent, and adjacent to the claim (not a vague 'may'/'helps' or fine print)?
detection.fail_anchor: Qualification only via 'may/helps', footnotes, or separated fine print.

rules.rule_text: Do not mischaracterize FDA approval or status (e.g., implying FDA endorsement of superiority or safety beyond the label).

detection.logic: Flag 'FDA[- ]approved' within 40 chars of safe|safest|best|only|superior|authentic and safe|proven; flag 'FDA[- ](cleared|approved)' for products whose meta.status != approved.
